title: A left orthogonal to a shift-stable class is replete and triangulated
statement: Let $\mathcal T$ be a pre-triangulated category [def-weil-triangulated-category], and let $\mathcal Q$ be any class of its objects stable under every integer shift: $Q\in\mathcal Q$ implies $Q[n]\in\mathcal Q$ for $n\in\mathbf Z$. Define ${}^{\perp}\mathcal Q$ to be the full subcategory on the objects $X$ such that every morphism $X\to Q$ is zero for every $Q\in\mathcal Q$. Then ${}^{\perp}\mathcal Q$ is replete (closed under isomorphisms) and triangulated: it contains zero objects, is stable under all integer shifts, and contains the third vertex of a distinguished triangle whenever it contains the other two. No smallness assumption on $\mathcal Q$ is required.
